name: biascorr
summary: Adam bias-correction inverse factors. Given step t (i32 scalar) and AttrBlob(beta1,beta2), outputs bc1_inv = 1/(1-beta1^t), bc2_inv = 1/(1-beta2^t). Implemented as a tiny 1-block kernel writing two f32 scalars.
contract: - step: i32 scalar (rank==0) OR i32 1D with shape[0]==1; contiguous required
- bc1_inv: f32 scalar (rank==0) OR f32 1D with shape[0]==1; contiguous required
- bc2_inv: f32 scalar (rank==0) OR f32 1D with shape[0]==1; contiguous required
- denominators are clamped by absolute value threshold 1e-20 to avoid inf/NaN
abi: - attr must exist, schema match, bytes>=8
- beta1 and beta2 must be non-NaN (beta==beta check)
notes: Kernel writes only if (blockIdx.x==0 && threadIdx.x==0); launch config is <<<1,32>>>.
Contiguity is required even for rank==0 scalars (current helper enforces d.contiguous).
Intended use: Adam optimizer step bias-correction factors (1/(1-b1^t), 1/(1-b2^t)).
Pow uses powf(beta, (float)t). Large t may underflow beta^t toward 0, which is fine.

variants.name: biascorr_f32_v0
supported: step: dtype=i32, scalar(0D) or 1D len=1, contiguous
bc1_inv: dtype=f32, scalar(0D) or 1D len=1, contiguous
bc2_inv: dtype=f32, scalar(0D) or 1D len=1, contiguous
notes: Thread0 computes t=max(step,1), b1t=powf(beta1,t), b2t=powf(beta2,t), then outputs inverses with denom clamp.

suites.name: basic_values
suites.desc: Bias-correction correctness across typical Adam betas and steps.

suites.name: supported_gating
suites.desc: Ensure attr and dtype/shape requirements are enforced.

experiments.title: Fast pow approximation for beta^t
experiments.change: Replace powf(beta, t) with exp2f(t * log2f(beta)) or precomputed log(beta) path; optionally handle beta near 1 with expm1 for better precision.
experiments.why: powf can be relatively heavy even though kernel is tiny; may matter if launched very frequently.
experiments.hypothesis: Lower kernel latency and improve optimizer step throughput when biascorr is executed per-step frequently.
experiments.proof: Profile kernel duration in nsys; compare against powf baseline; validate numerical agreement for typical beta/t ranges.
experiments.next: If step is always host-known, consider computing on host and passing scalars to fused optimizer kernel to remove this launch.

experiments.title: Fuse bias-correction into Adam update kernel
experiments.change: Compute (1/(1-b1^t), 1/(1-b2^t)) inside Adam update kernel, remove standalone biascorr op.
experiments.why: Standalone scalar kernel launch overhead can dominate; fusion reduces launches and sync points.
experiments.hypothesis: End-to-end optimizer step latency decreases, especially for small parameter tensors or many small ops.
experiments.proof: nsys launch count reduction; measure optimizer step time with/without fusion; correctness vs reference optimizer.
experiments.next: Make fusion conditional: only when Adam kernel already reads step/betas; keep biascorr op for modular paths.

measurements.notes: Report kernel launch+exec latency; bandwidth/TFLOPs not meaningful for scalar op.
